test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In May 2025, which of the following nodal agencies of the Union Government invited public comments on the Draft Framework of India’s Climate Finance Taxonomy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Economic Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency that invited public comments on the **Draft Framework of India’s Climate Finance Taxonomy** in **May 2025**.
 
• The primary objective of this framework is to provide a comprehensive **classification system** that defines which economic activities can be labeled as "sustainable" or "green" within the **Indian economy**.
 
• By establishing a clear taxonomy, the **Union Government** aims to mobilize large-scale **capital** toward climate-friendly projects while significantly reducing the risk of **greenwashing** in the financial markets.
 
• The draft was developed through extensive consultation with a **task force** that included representatives from the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, and the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**.
 
• This initiative is a critical step in aligning India's **financial sector** with its international commitments, such as those made under the **Paris Agreement** and the **Panchamrit** targets announced at **COP26**. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Department of Economic Affairs.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Climate Finance Taxonomy:**
 
 
• A **Taxonomy** acts as a dictionary for **investors**, **banks**, and **policymakers** to identify projects that contribute to **environmental objectives** like **climate change mitigation** and **adaptation**.
 
• The **India-specific taxonomy** focuses on sectors such as **Renewable Energy**, **Energy Efficiency**, **Sustainable Transport**, **Water and Waste Management**, and **Afforestation**.
 
• It helps in the issuance of **Sovereign Green Bonds**, which the **Government of India** began issuing in the **2022-23** financial year to fund **green infrastructure**.
 
 
 
• **Net Zero Target 2070:**
 
 
• India has committed to reaching **Net Zero emissions** by the year **2070**. Achieving this requires an estimated investment of **trillions of dollars** over the coming decades.
 
• The taxonomy ensures that **global and domestic investors** have the transparency needed to invest in **low-carbon technologies** and **resilient infrastructure**.
 
 
 
• **Roles of Other Agencies:**
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:** Acts as the premier **policy think tank** of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice but is not the lead for financial regulatory frameworks like the taxonomy.
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO):** Responsible for the **collection and analysis** of statistical data and the implementation of the **National Sample Survey**.
 
• **Department of Financial Services (DFS):** Handles issues related to **Banking**, **Insurance**, and **Pension Reforms**, supporting the broader fiscal goals of the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Convergence:** The **Draft Framework** ensures that **ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance)** reporting by Indian companies is standardized and consistent with **global best practices** like the **EU Taxonomy**.
 
• **Institutional Support:** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has also been active in this space, having released a **Framework for Acceptance of Green Deposits** in **2023** to encourage **sustainable finance** at the retail level.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By creating a regulated **green finance ecosystem**, India hopes to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** into **clean energy** sectors, which is vital for maintaining an **8% plus GDP growth rate** while decarbonizing the grid.
